terms.comment: Ancient uses commonly referred to the citron. Traupman records citreum for lemon. Morgan–Owens distinguishes its ancient citron reference from the later lemon use.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: numbered food and kitchen sections · Lewis & Short: citreum

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF: printed pp. 70–73 (food and drink), 124 (refrigerator), 280 (blender), 358 (peanut butter), 383 (spinach). Printed page numbers are one less than PDF page numbers in this copy. The blender entry on printed p. 280 was also checked against its rendered page; p. 71.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
